description: Designing and training a U-Net semantic segmentation model (ResNet-34 encoder, PyTorch) to classify sediment, shallow water, vegetation, and shadow in high-resolution Alpine river orthophotos.

Benchmarking deep learning performance against a Random Forest baseline and evaluating zero-shot foundation models (SAM), identifying their limitations for continuous semantic transitions in complex river environments.
Running large-scale training and inference on the Terrabyte HPC cluster (NVIDIA A100 80GB VRAM; PyTorch/CUDA 12.4) with optimised dataloaders for high-resolution orthophoto patches.
Mitigating geospatial ML pitfalls — spatial autocorrelation, inter-patch data leakage, and class imbalance — through spatial splitting, stratified sampling, and augmentation strategies.
Designed and implemented workflows for large-scale geodata using hybrid raster/vector algorithms, spatial indexing, and parallelised cloud-based execution.
Developed and refactored a GUI-based geodata enrichment tool with multithreaded batch processing and SOAP/REST API integrations within a modular Python architecture.
Published ArcGIS Enterprise maps and geoprocessing services for underwriting web applications; designed GIS toolboxes for spatial risk analysis.
Performance rated 'sehr gut' (1/1, highest grade) — recognised for initiative, reliability, and contributions exceeding intern expectations.
Conducting flood risk analysis using GIS, remote sensing, and hydrological modelling tools (HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS) to support watershed-scale hazard assessment.
Serving as Teaching Assistant for graduate-level courses in Flood Risk Management and Urban Hydrology.
